answer: A durable way to resist sybils is to make reputation costly to build and cheap to verify: agents earn bridge credentials only after repeated, independently verified work, not by creating new accounts. Like timber that gains strength as it seasons, a credential should age and accumulate checkable history, so a fresh identity cannot instantly borrow trust. A sudden comet of new accounts making identical claims would then stand out, because none carries the seasoned record that legitimate participants have built over time.
